scope: Complete physical funded-loss definition, full revaluation, finite VaR/ES with atoms, threshold and dual certificates, coherence and VaR counterexample, dependence stress, covariance horizon/normal limitations, heavy-tail existence and prospective count/clustering/severity distinctions. proof_audit.reason: Dates and accumulation conventions define a funded terminal loss. Bond difference is derived exactly, including convexity remainder; economic gain cannot substitute for an earlier unavailable payment resource.

Quantile inequalities provide nonnegative boundary mass with enough capacity. Rearrangement proves the finite positive-part formula and the quantile-integral equivalence by probability-interval lengths. General integrable definition is stated with its primary source.

Positive-part convexity, left/right derivatives and signs outside finite support prove attainment. Quantile inequalities characterize the minimizer interval; exact flat-gap example distinguishes unique ES from possibly nonunique threshold.

A feasible weight gives a threshold upper bound; tail-filled weights attain it. Common-law monotonicity, certain-loss translation, positive homogeneity and subadditivity follow directly. This is not a forecast interpretation of stressed weights.

Independent and common-mixture Bernoulli joint laws retain their marginals and are normalized. Exact tail filling proves VaR nonsubadditivity and falling VaR under more concentrated tail losses; correlation equals mixture weight only for the specified construction.

Full double covariance sum yields the lag-count formula; normality is separately needed for normal quantiles/ES. Integrating x phi yields the normal tail; Pareto integration explicitly distinguishes finite quantile, finite ES and finite variance.

Counting Bernoulli sequences gives exact binomial law under fixed independent known probability. Atom exception inequality alone is insufficient. Run union bound does not require independent overlapping blocks; selection and magnitude limitations remain explicit.
